title: Emrys and the Deadline
premise: Paloma Kavanagh, a crash investigator who lost their family in the row-twelve disaster and now works unattributed cases to stay off the record, receives a burner phone that rings with a voice they know intimately: their sister's, dead for six years. The calls lead them into a conspiracy where the crash was engineered for market manipulation, and the same architects are preparing a second event timed to Frankfurt's opening bell. Hunted by both the conspirators and their own agency, Paloma must decide whether to expose the truth and finally claim their identity—or trade their silence, and the secret of who really caused the crash, for a chance to save the passengers of flight 447. In the end, Paloma broadcasts the evidence minutes before markets open, sacrificing their anonymity forever but finding, at last, a place to belong among the living.
about_author: Ansel Winterbourne is a former aviation insurance adjuster who spent a decade reading black-box transcripts before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse in the Azores, where no plane has ever crashed twice.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Working a routine unattributed case in Lisbon, Paloma finds a burner phone sealed in evidence that rings with their dead sister Aoife's voice, reciting details of row twelve no report ever contained. Shaken, they verify the phone's serial doesn't exist in any registry. The emotional beat is grief cracked open—the careful invisibility Paloma built begins to fracture as the past demands acknowledgment.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Revisited
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Paloma and a shadowy fixer named Voss. Following the phone's coordinates, Paloma uncovers that the original crash was a staged short-selling scheme, and a second 'event' is scheduled before Frankfurt opens at 3:00 a.m. EST. Voss offers Paloma silence in exchange for the one document proving who ordered it. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve: duty and love pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: What the Markets Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, racing through Frankfurt's pre-dawn financial district. Betrayed by their own agency liaison, hunted by Voss's team, Paloma realizes the second target is a charter carrying survivors' families—including Aoife's daughter, alive all along under witness protection. Cornered on a rooftop above the exchange, Paloma must choose: hand over the secret or transmit it. The climax lands as they hit send with ninety seconds to spare.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, weeks later. The markets convulsed, the conspirators are indicted, and Paloma—now named, credited, and unable to hide—meets her niece Nell at a memorial for row twelve. Aoife's voice on the final call is revealed as a coerced recording, but the love it carried was real. The resolution's beat is quiet belonging: Paloma signs their name to the official report for the first time, visible at last.
